question: Do early-stage names on the incentive board, meaning a non-price incentive present (news, a material 8-K, an M&A filing naming the name as subject, a news halt, short-dated call flow or large option prints) and a price 0-10% above the reference close, earn a positive net return over the engine's X2 one-hour hold on Alpaca paper, and more than gain-matched controls without any non-price incentive?
why_forward: Several board components have no usable history: option-trade flow is recorded from 2026-09-24 (Alpaca OPRA history starts 2024-02 and has no receive times), and halt and news receive times exist only from the monitor's first day. A prospective paper study is therefore the first honest test; it is preregistered here before any order and is never tuned on its own outcomes.

selection.order: score descending, then relative volume descending (missing last), then symbol
selection.note: The board's own stage label is not used; the gain range is checked on a fresh SIP snapshot taken after the decision time. volatility_halt (a price-triggered pause) is scored by the board but does not count as a non-price incentive.

controls.pool: names in the same fresh full-market snapshot that pass every price, spread, dollar-volume, gain, liveness and symbol filter and have no non-price incentive component at the decision (monitor board.json incentive_symbols, which lists every symbol with any component other than relvol, regardless of score)
controls.count: 4 per selected name from its gain bucket, drawn without replacement across the session's selections
controls.draw: ascending sha256(protocol id | session date | decision time | symbol)
controls.outcome: SIP 1-minute bars after the session: open of the first bar that starts strictly after the selection record's snapshot_completed_at, to the open of the bar 60 minutes later, less a round-trip cost of twice the cost table's half-spread for the name's cell (rules.time_bucket of the decision time, rules.price_tier of the snapshot price, rules.dv_tier of the snapshot day dollar volume) plus rules.sell_fees on the exit

execution.engine: adaptive-paper mover trial mode (blueprints/us-equities/adaptive-paper, merged #172); the scan's protocol field stays the engine's execution protocol mover-early-entry-v1-20260924 and its source field names this study
execution.exit: X2 (60 minutes after the first entry fill)
execution.account: isolated Alpaca paper account (alpaca-paper-2) with its own engine state root, so these sessions, sizing equity and loss budgets are not shared with other mover trials
execution.bound_code: each selection record carries the sha256 of monitor.py, board_scan.py, this protocol, the engine config and the written scan, and is written before the scan

outcomes.primary: per round trip, net return = (exit fill value - entry fill value - rules.sell_fees on the exit, fees.json sha256 fa1f468b80f78dc0c050948123116f577e38ae9f8c03f9fb360d11042a3fed3d) / entry fill value, from the engine receipt's fills; Alpaca paper charges no commission and fills at quotes, so spread cost is inside the fills
secondary: mean control-matched difference: selected model return minus the mean of its matched controls' model returns (both on the controls' outcome definition)
outcomes.session_unit: a trading day (both decisions of a day belong to one session)
outcomes.analysis_point: exactly once, after the first trading day at whose end at least 20 sessions with a started decision and at least 100 completed round trips exist; no interim test is run
outcomes.estimator: pooled mean of per-round-trip net returns over the sessions in the sample
outcomes.test: circular block bootstrap over sessions in calendar order, blocks of 5 sessions, B = 20000 resamples of the same session count; each resample's statistic is the pooled mean of the round trips in its sessions (sessions without trades contribute none); one-sided 95% lower bound = 5th percentile (numpy.percentile, method linear); RNG numpy.random.default_rng(int(sha256(id).hexdigest()[:16], 16))
outcomes.pass: lower bound > 0 and the secondary mean difference > 0

stop_rules: the engine's own lifetime gross-loss and drawdown budgets (1000 USD) and its drawdown pause (beyond 20% pauses entries for that and the next nine engine sessions)
three consecutive trading days that each end with a needs_attention receipt
any parameter or code change bound in the selection record, which starts a new protocol version instead
missed_sessions: a stale board, an early or late run, or a refused scan writes a refusal record; such decisions count as sessions without trades
gate_relation: A pass is paper performance evidence for strategy-paper-performance. The live gate also requires strategy-historical-holdout, which this study cannot supply for its history-less components; whether a preregistered forward period may stand in for that holdout is an open gate decision, not assumed here.
amendments_before_first_order: 2026-09-24, from the independent pre-outcome review (no order placed yet): volatility_halt removed from the non-price list; controls restricted to names without any non-price incentive and matched on gain bucket; the control outcome window starts after the snapshot completes; a single analysis point, estimator, bootstrap, RNG, fees and cost table fixed; rung schedule extended to 400 engine sessions and the configs pinned by sha256; code, config and scan hashes recorded before the scan; a 300 s late guard and refusal records; M&A filings credited to the subject only; monitor state restored from its files after a restart, with its start time and stream downtime recorded.
limitations: the board score is a heuristic detector fixed on 2026-09-24 without outcome data
relative volume assumes a linear volume clock, so it reads higher at 10:30 than at 13:30 for the same activity
some Benzinga articles are themselves price-driven (movers lists), so the news component is partly price-derived
session option totals and news windows depend on the monitor's uptime; restarts restore them from the monitor's files, and each record carries the monitor start time and stream downtime
paper fills are simulated by Alpaca and can differ from live fills
two decisions per session share market conditions, so sessions (not trades) are the bootstrap unit
